resources.name: "GTFS Best Practices now available!" by Sean Barbeau
resources.desc: Discusses some of the challenges of an open data format like GTFS and the GTFS Best Practices that were launched in early 2017 to help address data quality.

resources.name: "What's new in GTFS-realtime v2.0" by Sean Barbeau
resources.desc: Discuss the shortfalls in GTFS-realtime v1.0 and the improvements in v2.0.

resources.name: "AVL, CAD, and Real-Time Passenger Info for Beginners" by Tony Laidig
resources.desc: Provides a general introduction to technology used to track vehicles.

resources.name: "Visualizing Better Transportation: Data & Tools" by Steve Pepple
resources.desc: A collection of transportation-related data and tools for the San Francisco Bay Area and other cities in North America, originally collected and discussed at a 2018 Transit Week Event at ARUP in San Francisco.

resources.name: "How to use GTFS data to track transit vehicles in realtime" by Tom Camp
resources.desc: Using GTFS and GTFS Realtime to provide continuous realtime updates.

resources.name: Tang et al. - "Ridership effects of real-time bus information system: A case study in the City of Chicago"
resources.desc: Experiment in Chicago, IL showed modest increase in ridership when riders had access to real-time info via text message or email.

resources.name: Kay et al. - "When(ish) is my bus? User-centered Visualizations of Uncertainty in Everyday, Mobile Predictive Systems"
resources.desc: Paper attempts to answr the question of "how do we communicate uncertainty in transit predictions?" Explains the problem, existing solutions and designs a better interface for letting users know when to arrive at the bus stop.

resources.name: Watkins et al. - "Where Is My Bus? Impact of mobile real-time information on the perceived and actual wait time of transit riders"
resources.desc: Experiments in Seattl,e WA showed that riders perceived shorter bus wait times when they had access to real-time info via mobile apps.

resources.name: Brakewood et al. - “An experiment evaluating the impacts of real-time transit information on bus riders in Tampa, Florida”
resources.desc: Controlled experiment in Tampa, FL showed that riders with access to real-time info via mobile apps perceived nearly 2 minute reduction in wait times compared to riders without real-time info. Riders with real-time info also had decreases in anxiety and frustration and better reception of agency.

resources.name: Brakewood et al. - "The impact of real-time information on bus ridership in New York City"
resources.desc: Experiment in NYC showed that ridership increased on long routes when real-time info was made available to riders.

resources.name: Higgins et al. - "Calculating place-based transit accessibility: Methods, tools and algorithmic dependence" (2022)
resources.desc: Compares software tools for calculating accessibility by walking and public transit including ArcGIS Pro, Emme, R5R, and OpenTripPlanner.

resources.name: Aemmer et al. - "Measurement and classification of transit delays using GTFS-RT data"
resources.desc: Presents a method for extracting transit performance metrics from a General Transit Feed Specification’s Real-Time (GTFS-RT) component and aggregating them to roadway segments. Used with Transit Vis, viewable here.

resources.name: APTA Policy Development and Research - Public Transportation Embracing Open Data
resources.desc: APTA's discussion of the benefits and challenges of open transit data (a short summary of the below TCRP report).

resources.name: TCRP G-16 Development of Transactional Data Specifications for Demand-Responsive Transportation (In progress)
resources.desc: The objective of this research is to develop technical specifications for transactional data for entities involved in the provision of demand-responsive transportation. Expected completion date is late 2018.
